problem.problem:
Bob is blue. Bob is round. Erin is nice. Erin is round. Erin is smart. Gary is not young. Harry is blue. Harry is furry. Harry is nice. Harry is round. All smart things are furry. Young, nice things are furry. If something is furry then it is young. Round, nice things are not quiet. All round things are smart. If Bob is young then Bob is nice. If something is smart and not young then it is blue.

Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
Bob is not nice.
raw_logic_programs:
Predicates:
Blue($x, bool) ::: Is x blue?
Round($x, bool) ::: Is x round?
Nice($x, bool) ::: Is x nice?
Smart($x, bool) ::: Is x smart?
Young($x, bool) ::: Is x young?
Furry($x, bool) ::: Is x furry?
Quiet($x, bool) ::: Is x quiet?

Facts:
Blue(Bob, True) ::: Bob is blue.
Round(Bob, True) ::: Bob is round.
Nice(Erin, True) ::: Erin is nice.
Round(Erin, True) ::: Erin is round.
Smart(Erin, True) ::: Erin is smart.
Young(Gary, False) ::: Gary is not young.
Blue(Harry, True) ::: Harry is blue.
Furry(Harry, True) ::: Harry is furry.
Nice(Harry, True) ::: Harry is nice.
Round(Harry, True) ::: Harry is round.

Rules:
Smart($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: All smart things are furry.
Young($x, True) && Nice($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: Young, nice things are furry.
Furry($x, True) >>> Young($x, True) ::: If something is furry then it is young.
Round($x, True) && Nice($x, True) >>> Quiet($x, False) ::: Round, nice things are not quiet.
Round($x, True) >>> Smart($x, True) ::: All round things are smart.
Young(Bob, True) >>> Nice(Bob, True) ::: If Bob is young then Bob is nice.
Smart($x, True) && Young($x, False) >>> Blue($x, True) ::: If something is smart and not young then it is blue.

Query:
Nice(Bob, False) ::: Bob is not nice.
